reason: The cited evidence (E1–E4) shows that higher Nb content in TiHfZrNb alloys enhances passivation, reduces defect density, and improves corrosion resistance in Hanks' fluid, but it does not address thermal oxidation, surface hardness, or oxide layer stability under the proposed treatment.
premises: Thermal oxidation of TiHfZrNb at 400–600 °C forms a dense, Nb-enriched oxide layer.
A Nb-enriched oxide layer reduces point defect density and enhances passivation.
A Nb-enriched oxide layer improves corrosion resistance in aggressive fluids.
A Nb-enriched oxide layer increases surface hardness.
The oxide layer remains stable and adherent under aggressive conditions.
